title: ShopiQ canonical product
description: The shape a catalogue import must supply. This is a KNOWLEDGE model, not a table definition: one entry here becomes one row in `products` plus rows in `product_specs`, `product_images` and `inventory`. Nothing here creates a variant table — a configuration IS a product, and `product_family` is the only thing tying configurations together.

catalog_version.description: Semver for the dataset, not the software. Bump when the product set changes so an import can be traced back to what produced it.

demo_dataset.description: Catalog metadata, deliberately NOT a database column. Marks a dataset as illustrative so nobody mistakes it for real merchandising.

id.description: Stable import key, used as the product slug. Must not change between imports: order history, images and rules all reference it.

product_family.description: Logical grouping ONLY — there is no family table and no variant table. Every purchasable configuration is its own product row; this string is what lets the assistant say 'the 1 TB version' and find its sibling. Example: asus-tuf-a15 covers asus-tuf-a15-16gb-512gb and asus-tuf-a15-32gb-1tb.

category.description: A leaf slug from taxonomy.json. Validation rejects anything else, because a product in a category no rule names is a product nothing will ever recommend.

segments.description: From vocabulary.json segments, for this product's category.

configuration.description: What distinguishes this row from its siblings in the same product_family — the axes on which a shopper chooses. Example: { "ram_gb": 32, "storage_gb": 1024 }. Keys should also appear in specifications so they remain filterable.

selling_price.description: Becomes products.price. THE PRICE THE CUSTOMER PAYS COMES FROM THE DATABASE AT READ TIME, never from this file once imported.

inventory.description: Seed value only. Live availability is always read from the inventory table; the recommender treats this file as historical the moment it is imported.

specifications.description: Normalized keys from vocabulary.json. Numeric keys must carry NUMBERS, not strings with units — '16 GB' cannot be compared against 16 and would silently drop the product from every range filter.

performance.description: 1-10 per dimension. A recommendation signal, not a benchmark — see vocabulary.json.

attributes.description: The facts another product is matched against: { "socket": "AM5" }, { "memory_type": "DDR5", "form_factor": "DIMM" }, { "connector": "USB-C", "power_w": 65 }.

compatible_sizes.description: For carriers: a sleeve listing ["13", "14"] fits those display sizes.

compatible_accessory_types.description: Accessory kinds this product accepts, from vocabulary.json accessory_types.

claims.description: Explicit statements about other products or classes. A not_compatible_with claim is an exclusion and overrides every positive match.

relationships.description: Product-specific relationships, for the cases a category rule cannot express — 'a MacBook Air wants THIS hub'. Category-level rules in recommendations.json cover everything else, so this list should stay short.

reason.description: Shown to the customer. Must be a fact about the pairing, not a sales line.

images.description: Supplied by the import. NEVER invented: a placeholder URL that 404s is worse than no image, and an image of the wrong product is worse still.

colour.description: Names the finish this shot shows. This is where colour options come from — there is no colour column and no per-colour stock.

recommendation_profile.description: Hints that tune ranking for this product without touching global rules.

boost.description: Flat adjustment to the final score. Bounded on purpose: a boost large enough to override budget fit would let merchandising put an unaffordable product first.

hero.description: Prefer as the lead example of its family when several tie.

accessory_budget_ratio.description: Sensible accessory spend as a fraction of this product's price. Defaults to the global setting.

suppress_cross_sell.description: Never offer accessories alongside this. For products where it would be crass.
